name: Input validation
needs: users can send any data to my API
someone made themselves admin by adding a field to the request
validate form data on the server too
a huge request crashed my server
summary: Checking every piece of incoming data on the server against what you expect: type, length, format and allowed values. Anything else is rejected before your code uses it. Browser checks only help the user. Anyone can skip them.
need_when: Every form, API endpoint, webhook and file import.
skip_when: Never on the server. Even internal endpoints get called with bad data eventually.

ways.title: A schema at each endpoint
ways.how: Zod or Valibot (TypeScript), Pydantic (Python) or JSON Schema. Parse the body into the schema and use only the parsed result.
ways.tradeoff: Clear and typed. You need the habit of never reading the raw body after parsing.

ways.title: Your framework's forms or serializers
ways.how: Django forms or DRF serializers with explicit field lists, Rails strong parameters, Laravel validation.
ways.tradeoff: Built in. 'All fields' shortcuts bring back mass assignment.

ways.title: Database constraints as the last line
ways.how: NOT NULL, CHECK constraints, foreign keys, unique indexes and column lengths.
ways.tradeoff: Catches what code misses. Errors arrive late and are less friendly.

prompt:
Add server-side input validation to [endpoints/forms].

Requirements:
- Define a schema for each endpoint's input: types, required fields, max lengths, allowed values, number ranges.
- Reject unknown fields. Never copy request data straight onto a model. Set allowed fields one by one (no mass assignment of role, owner_id, is_admin or price).
- Cap request body size at [1 MB] unless the endpoint needs more.
- Use parameterized queries or the ORM everywhere. No SQL built from strings.
- Return 400 with a field-by-field message the UI can show. Don't echo raw input back into HTML.
- Add database constraints for the rules that must never break.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. Sending is_admin=true or a different owner_id in the body changes nothing.
2. A 10,000-character name is rejected with a clear message.
3. A body over the size cap returns 413.
4. Searching for ' OR 1=1 -- returns a normal empty result.
5. Every endpoint in the app is listed with its schema.
